sentence: This project studies how parent mental health leads to early substance use among youth and how genetic, family and environmental factors link to those pathways.
This project studies how stem cells differentiate into parietal cells in the stomach lining and how certain factors keep parietal cells working well.
This project studies the flexible regions of alpha-synuclein, a misfolded protein linked to Parkinson's disease, to understand harmful cellular interactions and toxicity.
This project uses machine learning on surveys and health records to find what predicts poor outcomes after revascularization surgery for chronic limb threatening ischemia.
This project studies aging, including late-life disability, dementia and family caregiving, and how social, environmental and biological factors shape health in older adults.
This project makes peptide nucleic acids and tests whether they can target and degrade the viral genome of hepatitis B virus in animal models.
This project runs a core facility that helps cancer researchers build and use genetically engineered mice, including with genome editing and embryonic stem cells.
This project uses single cell methods to study how the epigenome shapes differences among breast cancer cells in the level of one protein.
This project builds methods to find the people, tissues and cells that carry latent DNA viruses and to learn why infections affect people differently.
This project builds a rapid over-the-counter urine test that detects fentanyl without needing an instrument.
This project uses electroencephalography to test whether people at risk for suicide become cognitively overwhelmed under challenging life circumstances and make poor choices.
This project builds a three-dimensional virtual airway model to produce digital orthodontic airway plates for infants with airway obstruction and feeding difficulties.
This project studies the structure and molecular workings of the coronavirus exoribonuclease complex during genome replication and transcription.
This project studies how cancer and the nervous system interact, including how cancer might remodel neuronal populations, using neuroscience tools.
This project tests a therapy in non-human primates that targets virus in lymph nodes and the intestines to eliminate it from those areas.
This project studies how a signaling pathway helps macrophages remove cholesterol and slows plaque progression in atherosclerosis, using single-cell profiling and preclinical models.
This project studies how interactions between cells in the tumor microenvironment of pancreatic cancer suppress immune responses, using mouse models and patient derived organoids.
This project finishes developing a spinal fusion device made with silicon nitride, a material with antibacterial and bone integration properties, to reduce infection.
This project gets a triple quadrupole mass spectrometer to help detect drug molecules in blood and organs and support drug synthesis.
This project studies the metabolites and mechanisms by which a therapeutic diet reduces ocular deficits in a mouse model of multiple sclerosis.
